newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 26.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australian ten year bond yields open 10 basis points higher at 8.08 percent after U.S. Federal Reserve raises official interest rates 0.25 of a percentage point. Disappointment also seen after Treasurer Peter Costello announced the Wallis report would not be released until after April 7. ANZ also announced late on Tuesday it would cut a net 356 jobs from May 26.

Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Tuesday that talks were still continuing with Seven Network Ltd to try to settle litigation between Seven and Optus' pay-tv associate Optus Vision. Earlier there were reports that the talks between the two camps had broken down. "Talks are still continuing," Optus spokesman David Foster told Reuters. Foster said there was a deadline until 5 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Wednesday.
Australia's Hoyts Cinemas Group said it will invest US$50 million in Chile, including US$20 million on building five cinema complexes in Santiago with 49 screens.

Woolworths Ltd said on Tuesday that the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) had approved the company's expansion on the grocery wholesaling business through its unit Independent Wholesalers Pty Ltd.

The Melbourne-based casual clothing retailer will release its half year profit result sometime today. Managing director Peter Wilkinson resigned earlier this month to take the helm at David Jones Ltd.
